To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the methylation patterns of histones H3 Lys4, Lys9 and Lys27 are correlated with transcriptional activity of plant genes, that ATX1 is required for transcription at ATX1 target genes, but is not required for the repositioning of nucleosomes at the LTP-promoter in atx1 mutant plants.

‘We have shown that histone H3 lysine methylation patterns are gene- and tissue-specific, and that the histone methyltransferase ATX1 is involved in the establishment of a gene-specific chromatin environment’.
the methylation of lys-9 (H3) is correlated with transcriptionally inactive genes and the absence of nucleosomes at the LTP promoter in the mutant atx1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epigenetic control of gene expression in plant cells and with the molecular mechanisms underlying the ATX1 function.
the role of histone-tails in transcriptional control and chromatin organization in plant development.
the role of histone-tails modifications in transcriptional regulation and chromatin structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
methylation of histone-tails in plants, as in other eukaryotes, may be a general mechanism to mark active and inactive genes.
methylation patterns of histones in plant genes are complex, and that they may vary in different developmental and tissue contexts.
histone methylation marks are not a general ‘code’ but rather a complex system that can be read by specific proteins to interpret the chromatin status of genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATX1 is not essential for the maintenance of transcriptional activity at all ATX1-regulable loci.
the histone code is an important mechanism of epigenetic regulation in plants.
histone-tail lysine-methylation patterns of active and inactive plant genes are similar to those of their animal counterparts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the histone code in Arabidopsis is not static but rather dynamic, changing during the course of development and in different tissues.
the histone code is a dynamic and flexible mechanism for the regulation of gene expression in plants.
the histone code in plants is more complex and dynamic than in other organisms.
